newsitem.title: USA: Lott warns W. House on spending rise in budget.
newsitem.headline: Lott warns W. House on spending rise in budget.

text.p: U.S. Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott Wednesday warned President Clinton that Republicans could not go along with a significant increase in domestic spending in any balanced budget plan.

In a speech to an education group, the Mississippi Republican said he had heard Clinton's budget, to be sent to Congress Thursday, could include as much as $100 billion in new spending on non-defense discretionary programs over the next five years.
Speaking to reporters later, Lott said he had not seen the budget and did not know the specifics.
But he warned that Congress could not go along with spending of that magnitude.
"We could not do that, we'll have to find a way to cut that way back," Lott said.
Lott reiterated that he believed Congress and the White House may be able to work out a balanced budget deal this year.
